title: 2001 HMMT February General Round 2 Problem 7
statement: A real numbers \(x\) is randomly chosen in the interval \(\left[-15 \frac{1}{2}, 15 \frac{1}{2}\right]\). Find the probability that the closest integer to \(x\) is odd.

solutions.text: By using a graphical method, we can see that, for real \(x\) on \(\left[-n-\frac{1}{2}, n+\frac{1}{2}\right]\), \(n\) an even integer, the probability that the closest integer to \(x\) is odd is \(\frac{n}{2 n+1}\). The desired probability is \(\left(\frac{15}{31}\right)\).
